clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12393 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). The four numbered paragraphs (1-101 to 1-104) establish, effective November 16, 1982, a three-member board under section 9A of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 159a), direct a report within 30 days after creation, restate the section 9A(c) status-quo period of 120 days after creation, and provide that the board terminates ninety days after the report. The command to create the board was performed when the board was appointed, but under owner ruling 2026-10-21 the order is not treated as ended by that performance or by the report. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C) a report deadline is not an end: the command is functionally spent when the board reports, but the order remained on the books until this revocation. The actual report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence. The statutory standstill (status-quo period) is likewise a spent fact and not an end; paragraph 1-103 measures it from the creation of the board, effective November 16, 1982, for 120 days thereafter, so by the order's own terms it ran out on March 16, 1983 (a computed date, 120 days after November 16, 1982), whatever the report date was. This clause provides that the board terminates on or after the submission of its report. The report date is not held in this packet’s citable evidence, and the clause is read as a report-relative sunset that is functionally spent on the report date and not as the end, by analogy to owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C), which that ruling applies to report-relative sunsets of other boards; this analogy is a reading disclosed for the reviewer. No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 12393 (47 FR 51851, Federal Register of November 18, 1982; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Establishing an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Long Island Rail Road and Certain Labor Organizations and signed November 16, 1982. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain labor organizations. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 1 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (whole). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12393 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; the standstill ran, under paragraph 1-103, from the creation of the board effective November 16, 1982 for 120 days, that is to March 16, 1983 (a computed date); the report date is not recorded as a later event because no report text is among this packet's citable evidence, so the claim states the functional spending of the report command without a date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
